title: Helmbridge QBR: Inference Economics & Roadmap
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private deployments
summary: Quarterly business review focused on recent usage spike, cost variance in embeddings vs chat, latency pain on 8k+ token requests, tradeoffs for moving critical flows to Dedicated or Private, and alignment on next-step pilot for quantization and VPC pen test. Agreed to run two benchmarks and share pricing scenarios and SOC2/ISO artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, Luca and Sofia are here too. we got about an hour, wanted to run through the QBR, usage, cost, reliability, and a quick roadmap sync.
[00:18] Alex Navarro: thanks, Maya. quick context, since last QBR we turned on a new embed pipeline and saw a big jump in token volume, some of that's batch and some interactive. overall pleased but the bill surprised some folks.
[00:32] Priya Singh: yes sorry to jump in — the finance team flagged a 42% month over month increase and they want options.
[00:40] Luca Romano: okay noted. first, can we confirm where most of the spend is — embeddings vs chat generation?
[00:48] Michael Ortiz: embeddings, mostly. the new search embeddings are at high QPS, and we also have some long-context summarization in a background job.
[00:56] Sofia Alvarez: also saw a lot of small repeated calls that could benefit from caching.
[01:04] Maya Chen: right, caching and batching suggestions are low hanging fruit. we can run a prefix KV cache eval and a batching config that may reduce token counts by 20-40% depending on pattern.
[01:18] Alex Navarro: can you spell that out? we were worried caching would add staleness.
[01:24] Luca Romano: totally — prefix caching only for deterministic embeddings and for the chat we'd use a TTL + content-hash approach. for summarization jobs we can cache at the chunk-level to avoid re-tokenizing.
[01:40] Priya Singh: beyond caching, what about model choices? are there cheaper model variants for embeddings that don't degrade quality?
[01:46] Luca Romano: yes, there's lower-cost quantized variants and smaller embedding models. we can run a quality sweep on your eval set. typically for search you can drop to a 6B quantized without major recall loss, but we should test.
[02:00] Michael Ortiz: and what about latency — our user-facing summarization needs 200-400ms p95. currently some requests to 8k tokens are spiking into seconds.
[02:10] Maya Chen: 8k tokens will hit context-scaling limits. options are: reduce sequence length via pre-filtering, move those flows to a Dedicated pool with pinned capacity, or use longer-context optimized kernels and higher memory GPUs. Dedicated gives better tail latency but requires a commit.
[02:28] Dana Li: from a security perspective, Dedicated is fine but we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS; we also need audit logs shipped to our SIEM.
[02:38] Sofia Alvarez: we do support VPC/private with customer KMS and audit export. we'll share the SOC2 apendix and the audit-log schema.
[02:48] Alex Navarro: timeline — if we decide to pilot Dedicated, how long to provision?
[02:54] Maya Chen: for dedicated capacity typically 3-5 business days to provision and validate, depending on region and SKU availability; private on-prem is longer.
[03:04] Priya Singh: finance question again — committed capacity pricing vs pay-as-you-go, can you show scenarios?
[03:10] Luca Romano: yes we'll produce three scenarios: conservative (no commit), mid (monthly reserved), and aggressive (annual commit). math will include unit token costs, amortized GPU hours, and an ops buffer.
[03:20] Alex Navarro: okay, show me the break-even point.
[03:22] Maya Chen: we'll add that to the follow-up deck.
[03:26] [03:26] Alex Navarro: (mutter) please don't make the spreadsheet too academic.
[03:32] Luca Romano: ha — understood.
[03:34] [06:05] Priya Singh: curious about rollout risk — if we move some flows to Dedicated and a node goes down, what's your fallback?
[06:12] Luca Romano: we have smart routing with automatic fallback to hosted compatible model variants and cross-region failover; we can configure canaries so only a small percentage route to the new pool initially.
[06:24] Dana Li: and do you surface detailed traces so our SREs can correlate latency spikes to model versions?
[06:30] Sofia Alvarez: yes, per-request tracing and token-level latency breakdowns are available in Redwood Console; we can emit spans to your tracing backend as well.
[06:42] Michael Ortiz: about quantization — we tried int8 on prem and saw small regressions. how do you measure quality drift?
[06:48] Luca Romano: we integrate eval hooks: you can tie QA prompt sets to alerts and regressions trigger rollback or degrade to a higher precision variant. we'll run the eval on your dev set during the pilot.
[06:58] Alex Navarro: what's the ops burden for that? we don't want to chase regressions constantly.
[07:03] Sofia Alvarez: we do automated rollbacks and can set thresholds; the SE team will help configure initial thresholds so it's low maintenance.
[07:12] [10:15] Priya Singh: legal asked for data residency controls — some customer PII must stay in EU regions only. can you guarantee region pinning?
[10:24] Maya Chen: yes you can pin routes to region and we support private deployments in EU region; for strict residency we recommend Private with VPC and on-prem as needed.
[10:36] Dana Li: and what about encryption at rest and KMS integrations?
[10:40] Sofia Alvarez: we integrate with common KMS providers and support customer-managed keys; we will provide the KMS whitepaper.
[10:48] Michael Ortiz: ok good.
[11:02] [15:00] Alex Navarro: on reliability — last month we saw 3 incidents affecting search, root cause was a cascade when a background job retried too aggressively and overloaded the gateway.
[15:12] Luca Romano: common pattern — we recommend circuit breakers and rate limiters at the client side, plus batching at the gateway. also suggest backpressure and retry-with-jitter.
[15:24] Priya Singh: can Redwood help implement the rate limiting pattern? our infra team is stretched.
[15:30] Maya Chen: absolutely — we offer runbook templates and an onboarding engagement; SEs can pair with your platform engineer to instrument.
[15:38] Michael Ortiz: we need an SLA on tail latency for priority routes. what does Redwood offer?
[15:44] Sofia Alvarez: Dedicated contracts include latency SLOs and an uptime SLA; hosted tier has best-effort latency but enterprise customers can get SLO add-ons. we'll include the SLO table in the follow-up.
[15:56] Alex Navarro: ok.
[16:02] [22:10] Priya Singh: roadmap talk — Redwood's upcoming features you mentioned in the notes, anything we should plan around?
[22:18] Luca Romano: next quarter we're rolling out an improved long-context runtime with kernel selection optimizations, plus more aggressive KV cache primitives and a first-class quantized model catalog.
[22:36] Maya Chen: also a new console view for per-route cost attribution and per-token cost drilldowns.
[22:44] Alex Navarro: that per-route cost view would be huge for us.
[22:48] Priya Singh: timeline?
[22:50] Luca Romano: pilot next month, GA in about 2 quarters. we can give you access to the pilot if you want early visibility.
[22:58] Michael Ortiz: yes please. trial access would help our finance and infra teams validate.
[23:04] [30:00] Dana Li: security review — we'll need the SOC2 report, pen test schedule, and evidence of access controls for RBAC/SSO.
[30:08] Sofia Alvarez: we have a security pack; I'll share the doc links after the call and we can set up a security deep dive with our security engineer.
[30:18] Alex Navarro: are there known customer restrictions with integrating our SIEM?
[30:22] Sofia Alvarez: generally none; we support syslog, S3 export, and direct API pushes.
[30:28] Priya Singh: ok, good.
[30:32] [37:45] Michael Ortiz: ok let's talk about concrete pilots: 1) embeddings cost reduction test with quantized 6B vs current model, 2) Dedicated pilot for the 8k summarization path, 3) caching and rate-limit runbook implementation.
[37:56] Maya Chen: sounds good. we'll scope two benchmarking runs for #1 and #2, one on your dev dataset and one synthetic for tail latency.
[38:06] Luca Romano: also would like to run an end-to-end A/B for quality on the quantized embeddings.
[38:12] Alex Navarro: what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated pilot?
[38:18] Maya Chen: we can do a short-term reserved pool (2 week pilot) with pro-rata billing; if you expand to monthly/annual commit it's discounted.
[38:28] Priya Singh: finance will need the pro-forma.
[38:32] Maya Chen: we'll send that.
[38:36] [45:00] Alex Navarro: last item — support model, on-call and escalation. we need a clear RTO/RPO for priority failures.
[45:10] Sofia Alvarez: enterprise support includes 24/7 escalation with named SE on-call and a joint runbook; we can propose an on-call SLA in the contract.
[45:20] Dana Li: can you provide an audit of who accessed customer data historically? for compliance audits.
[45:26] Sofia Alvarez: yes we have audit logs with user principal and action, we'll provide export examples.
[45:34] [53:10] Priya Singh: let's recap and next steps.
[53:15] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to deliver follow-up deck with pricing scenarios and break-even; security pack and SOC2 artifacts; two benchmark plans (quantized embeddings and Dedicated long-context latency); trial access to the console pilot; scheduling security deep dive and SE pairing.
[53:34] Alex Navarro: agreed.
[53:38] Michael Ortiz: one ask — please include realistic cost delta examples not just percentages.
[53:44] Maya Chen: will do.
[53:48] Priya Singh: thanks everyone, good session.
[53:52] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll send notes and action items.
[53:58] [57:50] (call ends)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing scenarios and break-even analysis (Maya) - 2026-11-12
SE pairing session to implement rate-limiter/runbook with Michael - schedule week of 2026-11-15
Provision pilot Dedicated pool (2-week) if approved by Helmbridge finance - target start 2026-11-22
Share security pack, SOC2, audit-log schema and KMS whitepaper (Sofia) - 2026-11-09
Give Helmbridge pilot access to console cost view (Luca) - 2026-11-13
action_items: Maya Chen: prepare pricing scenarios and pro-forma for Dedicated vs PAYG - due 2026-11-12
Sofia Alvarez: send security pack, SOC2, and audit-log export examples - due 2026-11-09
Luca Romano: scope and schedule two benchmarks (quantized embeddings quality + long-context latency) - due 2026-11-13
Michael Ortiz: share dev eval dataset and example queries for benchmarking - due 2026-11-10
Alex Navarro: confirm finance decision window for pilot commit - due 2026-11-16
